summary: Composio already runs a managed Notion OAuth app, so you can connect users today without registering anything. You only need your own app if you want your branding on the consent screen or a separate rate-limit budget. To build your own, create a "public connection" in Notion's new Developer portal: choose capabilities (Notion has no OAuth scopes), add Composio's redirect URI, and copy the client ID and secret. The biggest gotcha is the installation scope. You set it once at creation ("Any workspace" or "Selected workspaces only") and can't change it later. Pick "Any workspace" if arbitrary users must connect. Also, Notion's docs say the Authorization URL field only fills in after you submit the connection for review, so plan for a possible review step before broad use.

verdict.difficultyReason: Creating the connection is self-serve and takes minutes. But the current docs tie the Authorization URL to a review submission, and Marketplace listing needs a Notion review (5-10 business days), so broad rollout may involve a light review.

devReady.estimate: 15-30 min (0 min with Composio's managed app)
devReady.detail: Create a public connection, add Composio's redirect URI, paste the client ID and secret into a Composio auth config, then authorize your own workspace. Each user picks which pages the connection can see. Pages they don't pick are invisible to the API.

productionReady.detail: Notion's docs say an 'Any workspace' public connection 'can be used via its OAuth flow without being listed.' But the Authorization URL field only fills in after you submit for review, so you may have to submit before outside users can connect. The docs give no timeline for that review. A Marketplace listing is optional, and Notion says to expect a reply 'within 5-10 business days via email.' 'Selected workspaces only' connections can only be installed by the workspaces you chose at creation.

verdict.handsOnEffort: 30 min-2 hours (more if you write a Marketplace listing)

nextAction: To prototype, connect Notion now through Composio's managed auth. For your own app, open https://app.notion.com/developers/connections and go to Build > Public connections > Create new connection. Choose installation scope "Any workspace" and add the redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add.

phases.title: Register the public connection
phases.goal: You have an OAuth client ID and secret with Composio's redirect URI registered

steps.title: Open the Developer portal
steps.detail: Sign in to Notion and go to the Developer portal. In the sidebar, open Build > Public connections and click 'Create new connection'.

steps.title: Fill in basic fields
steps.detail: Enter a connection name, choose a development workspace, and set the installation scope to 'Any workspace' (you can't change it later). Optionally add a public Notion template page URL that users can duplicate during authorization.

steps.title: Select capabilities
steps.detail: Notion has no scope strings. Tick the capabilities your agent needs: read content, update content, insert content, comment read/insert, and user info (with or without email). Keep the list minimal. Users see these on the consent screen.

steps.title: Add the redirect URI
steps.detail: Under OAuth configuration, add https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. If you register more than one URI, the token request must include redirect_uri. Composio handles this.

steps.title: Copy credentials
steps.detail: Open the Configuration tab and copy the OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret. Keep the secret private.

phases.title: Connect through Composio and test
phases.goal: You complete an OAuth flow with your own workspace and make API calls

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config
steps.detail: In https://dashboard.composio.dev go to Auth Configs > Create Auth Config > Notion > OAuth2. Paste the client ID and secret, click Create, and copy the ac_... ID.

steps.title: Pass the auth config in your session
steps.detail: Set authConfigs: { notion: 'ac_...' } in the session. Toolkits you don't list keep using managed auth.

steps.title: Authorize and pick pages
steps.detail: Run the connect flow. Notion redirects to app.notion.com/install-integration. Choose pages in the page picker and approve. The connection can only see the pages you share.

steps.title: Smoke-test the API
steps.detail: Call search or retrieve a page with the new connection. Confirm that refresh works: each refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token.

phases.title: Go live
phases.waitTime: Review for the Authorization URL: no published timeline. Marketplace: 5-10 business days.

steps.title: Submit the connection for review if the portal requires it
steps.detail: Notion's docs say 'The Authorization URL field populates after a public connection is submitted for review.' If outside workspaces can't install, submit from the portal. Composio builds the authorize URL itself (client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, owner=user).

steps.title: Test with a second, unrelated workspace
steps.detail: Authorize from a workspace that isn't your development workspace. This confirms that 'Any workspace' installs work.

steps.title: Optional: create a Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Under Listings > Connections, click 'Start a new connection listing'. Add the name, description, category, tags, images and logo, link the connection, then submit. Notion replies by email in 5-10 business days.

steps.title: Store rotated refresh tokens
steps.detail: Every refresh issues a new refresh token. Replace the stored one each time. Composio does this for you.

steps.title: Handle 429s
steps.detail: Respect the Retry-After header. The limit is 180 requests per minute per connection (600 on Business/Enterprise), plus a per-workspace limit. Data source queries are limited to about 3 requests per second.

scopes.purpose: Read pages, databases and blocks the user shared
scopes.reviewNote: No separate review. Shown on the consent screen.

Create new pages, blocks and database rows

scopes.reviewNote: No documented extra review. Expect questions during a Marketplace review if you don't justify it.

blockers.title: Wrong installation scope
blockers.symptom: Users from other workspaces can't install, or the connection is not eligible for the Marketplace
blockers.fix: You can't change the scope. Create a new connection with 'Any workspace' and update the Composio auth config.

blockers.title: Authorization URL empty in the portal
blockers.symptom: The Configuration tab shows no Authorization URL
blockers.fix: Notion only fills it in after you submit for review. Submit the connection, or let Composio build the URL from the client ID and redirect URI.

blockers.title: Agent sees no content
blockers.symptom: Search returns empty results, or the API returns object_not_found
blockers.fix: The user didn't share those pages in the page picker. Ask them to reconnect and choose more pages, or add the connection to a page from its ••• > Connections menu.

blockers.title: Redirect URI mismatch
blockers.symptom: An error at authorize or token exchange
blockers.fix: Register exactly https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. If you register several URIs, redirect_uri must be sent in the token request.

blockers.title: Marketplace rejection
blockers.symptom: A rejection email after 5-10 business days
blockers.fix: Fix any brand/trademark misuse (for example, 'Notion' in your app name) or the quality issues they cite, then resubmit.

blockers.title: Rate limiting
blockers.fix: Back off using Retry-After. A custom app separates your quota from Composio's shared one.

technical.pkce: Not documented for api.notion.com. Use a confidential client with the client secret. The separate Notion MCP server (mcp.notion.com) advertises S256 PKCE and dynamic client registration, but that is a different OAuth server.
technical.refreshTokens: The token response includes access_token, refresh_token, bot_id, owner and workspace info. Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token. Each refresh rotates both tokens. No access-token lifetime is published.
technical.redirectUriRules: Redirect URIs are registered in the connection's OAuth configuration. redirect_uri must be sent at token exchange if it was in the authorize URL or if several URIs are registered. Wildcard support is not documented.
technical.notes: No scope parameter: permissions come from the capabilities set on the connection, plus each user's page picker. The authorize URL needs owner=user and response_type=code. The token endpoint uses HTTP Basic auth (base64 client_id:secret). One token is issued per user/workspace install (a bot), and each user must authorize separately. Notion now uses the term 'connections' instead of 'integrations'. Old URLs like notion.so/profile/integrations redirect to app.notion.com.

drafts.title: Marketplace listing description
drafts.content: [APP_NAME] is an AI assistant that works with your Notion workspace. Once connected, it can read the pages and databases you choose to share, summarize them, answer questions, and create or update pages and database entries when you ask. [APP_NAME] only accesses pages you explicitly select in Notion's page picker, and you can revoke access at any time from Settings > Connections. Support: [SUPPORT_EMAIL]. Privacy policy: [PRIVACY_URL].

drafts.title: Capability justification / reviewer notes
drafts.content: Capabilities requested: Read content, Update content, Insert content[, Read/Insert comments]. Read content lets the agent retrieve and search pages the user shared so it can answer questions. Insert content lets it create pages or database rows when the user asks (for example, meeting notes or tasks). Update content lets it edit properties or append blocks on request. We don't request user email access [or: we request user email to map Notion users to [APP_NAME] accounts]. Test steps: 1) Sign up at [APP_URL] with [TEST_ACCOUNT]. 2) Click 'Connect Notion' and share a test page. 3) Ask the agent to 'summarize my page' and 'add a task to my database'. Tokens are stored encrypted by our auth provider (Composio) and are deleted on disconnect.
